articleTitle: 27 Gbit/s photonic wireless 60 GHz transmission system using 16-QAM OFDM
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: In this paper, we present a simple architecture for a super-broadband 60 GHz photonic wireless system. Using a cascaded optical RF and data modulation approach, advanced photonic components and a high-spectral efficient QAM-OFDM modulation format, we realized a compact 60 GHz photonic wireless system having a spectral efficiency as large as 3.86 bit/s/Hz. By making use of the 7 GHz spectral bandwidth in the 60 GHz band which was opened up for unlicensed broadband wireless services worldwide, we achieved record data throughputs. For example, by using a 16-QAM OFDM subcarrier modulation, we experimentally demonstrate photonic wireless transmission of 27.04 Gbit/s with a mean EVM of 17.63%. Wireless experiments were carried out in a lab environment with a maximum transmit power of -1 dBm and 23 dBi gain antennas for a wireless span of 2.5 m. This can be extended to some 100 m span when using high-gain antennas and higher transmit power levels.

articleTitle: Data transmission using phase-shift keying on a 92 GHz carrier
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Wireless data transmission at 2.3 Gb/s, with binary phase-shift keying encoding, on a 92 GHz carrier is achieved using photonic components to generate and modulate the millimeter-wave. A high-speed photodiode is used to convert the doubly-modulated optical signal to a modulated millimeter-wave carrier. Two antennas are used to transmit and receive the data-encoded millimeter-wave signal. Millimeter-wave wireless signals are measured out to a distance of 890 meters.

articleTitle: Spurious-free dynamic range of a tunable delay line based on slow light in SOA
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We develop a model describing harmonic and intermodulation distortions in SOAs. This model, valid for any input spectrum, enables to derive the spurious-free dynamic range of a slowlight delay line based on coherent population oscillations.

articleTitle: Photonic generation of chirp-free UWB signals for UWB over fiber applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Highly chirped optical UWB pulses with wide optical spectral widths tend to be distorted by fiber dispersion, which is undesirable for UWB over fiber transmission systems. In this paper, we investigate theoretically and experimentally a method to generate in the optical domain stable chirp-free UWB signals with a narrow optical spectral width. The UWB pulse generator consists of a polarization modulator (PolM) and a polarization-maintaining fiber (PMF) based delay line. The generated UWB signals are transmitted over a 10- or 24-km optical standard single-mode fiber followed by a wireless link. Experimental results show that the system has a good tolerance to fiber dispersion.

articleTitle: Instantaneous photonic microwave frequency measurement with a maximized measurement range
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: The use of photonic techniques to achieve frequency-to-power mapping is very attractive for instantaneous microwave frequency measurement. To have a large measurement range and a uniform measurement resolution in the range, to accurately evaluate the center frequency of a continuous-wave (CW) as well as a pulsed microwave signal, and to easily perform calibration of the measurement system, a linear amplitude comparison function (ACF), defined as the ratio of two powers of the microwave signal experiencing different power fading, is highly desirable. In this paper, we propose and demonstrate, for the first time, a novel technique to achieve a linear ACF for microwave frequency measurement with a maximized measurement range. For a measurement resolution of ≅0.4 GHz, a measurement range of 0˜25 GHz is obtained for a CW microwave signal and a measurement range of 3˜18 GHz is achieved for a pulsed microwave signal. The system is potentially integratable in a monolithically chip, which have the desirable features of small size, low cost and stable operations.

articleTitle: Photonic microwave filter with single bandpass response based on Brillouin processing and SSB-SC
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A photonic structure for microwave filtering with single passband and the capability of continuously tuning the filter response over a broad microwave range is proposed and experimentally demonstrated. The scheme is based on using stimulated Brillouin scattering and single sideband modulation with suppressed carrier (SSB-SC).

articleTitle: Hybrid silicon tunable filter based on a Mach-Zehnder interferometer and ring resonantor
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A novel photonic integrated tunable filter on the hybrid silicon platform is proposed and demonstrated. The filter incorporates a ring resonator placed in one arm of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer making it possible to obtain programmable filter transfer function. The microwave and optical frequency responses were also characterized.

articleTitle: Low bit rate digital radio over fibre system
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A novel digital RoF system, which shows an equipment limited EVM of <3% range for 5 MHz bandwidth W-CDMA signals, is demonstrated. Using a compression technique this signal could be digitally transmitted at 7.68 Mbps.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of RF photonic downconversion from 4–40 GHz
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We present downconversion results using our coherent RF-to-bits photonic receiver. Single-digit decibel conversion loss is achieved into the millimeter-wave band. Digitization and linearity of the downconverted signal are also discussed.

articleTitle: 14 Gbps 60 GHz RoF link employing a simple system architecture and OFDM modulation
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A radio-over-fiber system with a simple architecture is used to transport a 14 Gbps OFDM signal occupying the full 60 GHz band. Fiber lengths exceeding 3 km are supported without any dispersion compensation.

articleTitle: A high-order FIR microwave photonic filter
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A new high-order, high-Q microwave photonic filter structure, is presented. Experimental results demonstrate a filter response with 158 taps, which is the highest number of taps for a microwave photonic FIR filter reported to date.

articleTitle: Modelling of a DFB laser at low bias directly modulated with an OFDM signal for RoF applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A DFB laser biased at a low bias point is modeled using a modified AM/AM Rapp model. Distortion effects are simulated and compared to the analytical predictions made by Bussgang's theorem for soft limiter nonlinearity.

articleTitle: Giga-bit wireless link using 300–400 GHz bands
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: This paper presents photonic generation of high-power continuous terahertz-wave signals at frequencies from 300 GHz to 400 GHz, and their application to giga-bit wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: High-current backside-illuminated InGaAs/InP p-i-n potodiode
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We proposed a high-current backside-illuminated InGaAs/InP p-i-n photodiode (PD) with a non-absorbing drift region, and demonstrated an RF power output of 29.0 dBm at 5 GHz, a 3-dB bandwidth of 7 GHz, and a third order intercept point of 31 dBm at 2 GHz using a 70-mum-diameter PD.

articleTitle: Traveling wave semiconductor cascade laser using wavelength division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a wavelength-division multiplexed traveling wave semiconductor cascade laser (WDM-TWSCL) for analog fiber-optic link applications. A four-element WDM-TWSCL has been constructed using commercially available components as a proof-of-concept. A return loss better than 10 dB has been achieved from DC to 3 GHz while the intensity modulation (IM) transfer function magnitude is seen to increase with increasing number of elements.

articleTitle: Mixed wireless communications and RFID sensor networks over fibre
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A second harmonic suppression scheme allowing RoF links to support communications and passive UHF RFID is reviewed. Using RoF distributed antenna system techniques, the coverage and location accuracy of passive UHF RFID are significantly improved.

articleTitle: Simple remote heterodyne RoF system for Gbps wireless access
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A simple method for distribution of radio over fiber mm-wave signals for gigabit wireless access is presented. By heterodyning two uncorrelated lasers, the mm-wave carrier can be freely adjusted. A broadband diode detector in the mobile unit allows envelope detection without a local oscillator and capability for multi-channel configurations.

articleTitle: 60 GHz bidirectional optical signal distribution system at 3 Gbps for wireless home network
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We propose and validate a new radio-over-fibre (RoF) home network architecture allowing a 60 GHz wireless signal bidirectional distribution, based on a set-up of new 60 GHz components (mode locked laser and reflective electro-absorption modulator).

articleTitle: Single-sideband electrooptic modulators and their application in tunable opto-electronic oscillators
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We report on the development of resonant single sideband electro-optical modulators using whispering gallery mode resonators made with electrooptic material. Application of these modulators in compact, widely tunable opto-electronic oscillators and all-optical atomic clocks is discussed.

articleTitle: Simplified millimeter-wave radio-over-fiber system using optical heterodyning of low-cost independent light sources and RF homodyning at the receiver
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A simplified, cost-effective millimeter-wave radio-over-fiber system is proposed by heterodyning two independent low-cost light-sources and RF homodyning at the receiver that suppresses phase-noise effects. Proposed system avoids phase/frequency locking, high-speed modulators and local oscillators/mixers in CO and BSs.

articleTitle: Optimisation of a microwave frequency discriminator based on an optical delay line
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A microwave frequency discriminator based on an optical delay line is studied. This system features a noise floor below -150 dBc/Hz at 10 kHz offset. The noise mechanisms are studied in order to determine the main noise contributors.

articleTitle: High power UTC photodiodes design and application for analog fiber optic links
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We report on the design and characterization of uni-traveling-carrier photodiodes (UTC-PDs) achieving simultaneously high speed (ges 20 GHz), high responsivity (0.83 A/W), and high saturation current (ges 80 mA). These performances yield attractiveness of the designed PDs for use in analog fiber optic links. Indeed, high power operation enhances both the RF link gain and dynamic range. This was experimentally confirmed by demonstrating a L-band direct modulation analog fiber optic link using the developed UTC-PDs. The demonstrated link exhibits an intrinsic gain close to -1 dB, and a compression to noise ratio as high as 162 dB.Hz at 10 mA of detected photocurrent.

articleTitle: Heterodyne locking of an integrated optical phase-locked loop
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We demonstrate proof-of-concept heterodyne locking of the first optical phase-locked loop photonic integrated circuit. The circuit contains two sampled-grating distributed reflector lasers monolithically integrated with optical amplifiers, multimode interference splitters/couplers, and high-speed modulators and photodetectors.

articleTitle: Low phase noise optical oscillator at 30Ghz using a quantum dash mode-locked laser associated with an optical self injection loop
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Quantum dash mode-locked laser are very simple sources to generate a low linewidth tone over an optical signal. Such a devices has been used to generate a tone at its third harmonic, at 30 GHz and integrated into an optical self-injection loop in order to get a low phase noise oscillator. A phase noise as low as -105 dBc/Hz at an offset frequency of 100 kHz has been obtained with such a source.

articleTitle: Experimental influence of the base load effect on SiGe/Si and InGaAs/InP HPTs
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Heterojunction bipolar phototransistors (HPTs) This paper presents an experimental direct validation of the opto-microwave matching properties of heterojunction bipolar phototransistors (HPTs) for the first time. Thus, it provides a direct validation of the associated theory and confirms that HPT require a special process to their base matching as it differs dramatically from conventional complex conjugate matching. This experimental study is undertaken up to 10 GHz on SiGe/Si phototransistors at 850 nm and on InGaAs/InP phototransistors at 1550 nm, with both the HPTs integrated in conventional HBT technologies for greater integration with electronic circuits.

articleTitle: Fiber-wireless DWDM networks and radio-over-fiber technologies
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Dense wavelength division multiplexing network of coexisting analog radio-over-fiber and digital fiber-to-the-home signals is presented, by focusing on enabling techniques including optical frequency interleaving, supercontinuum light source, and photonic dynamic channel allocation for wireless services.

articleTitle: The impact of RF nonliniearities in an optical link on the contrast of imaging radars
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: The contrast of imaging radars is shown to be severely limited by RF nonlinearities, introduced by opto-electronic devices like intensity modulators. Limitations on the allowable modulation index are studied for linearly-chirped pulses returned from clutter.

articleTitle: A wireless hybrid mode locked laser for low cost millimetre wave radio-over-fiber systems
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: This paper presents a novel hybrid mode locking technique where a planar antenna is combined with a mode locked laser and shows how hybrid mode locked lasers can be used to transmit baseband data.

articleTitle: Nonuniform photonic sampling techniques for broadband frequency identification
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We present the experimental results of a photonic analog-to-digital conversion testbed seeking to optimize the performance and applicability of nonuniform photonic sampling techniques.

articleTitle: Dynamic chirped microwave photonic filter
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A chirped single bandpass microwave photonic filter based on a broadband optical source, a Mach-Zehnder interferometer and a dispersive element is proposed. Special and unique features are shown such as the capacity of modifying the chirp in the passband using the dispersive element together in combination with the possibility of tunability and reconfigurability. The later features are achieved by means of a Mach-Zehnder interferometer and the power spectrum distribution of the optical source.

articleTitle: Multiple-beam optically controlled beamformer using spatial-and-wavelength division multiplexing
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We propose an optically controlled multiple-beam phased array antenna employing spatial and wavelength multiplexing. We have developed the prototype of the optical beam-former, which enables control of 10 beams individually, and demonstrated at 18 GHz.

articleTitle: Experimental analysis of two measurement techniques to characterize photodiode linearity
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: As photodiodes become more linear, accurately characterizing their linearity becomes very challenging. We compare the IMD3 results from a standard two tone measurement to those from a more complex three tone measurement technique. A Ge n-i-p waveguide photodetector on Silicon-on-Insulator (SOI) substrate is used for the comparison. Additionally, we analyze, via simulation, the limitations of the measurement system in determining the distortion of highly linear photodiodes.

articleTitle: Fourier transform optically controlled phased array antenna in receiving operation
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Optically controlled beam forming techniques are effective for phased-array antenna control. We have developed the Fourier transform optical beamformer (FT-OBF). In the FT-OBF, the antenna radiation pattern inputted into an amplitude only spatial light modulator is optically Fourier transformed to a specific phase-front light beam equivalent to an antenna excitation distribution. We developed the prototype of an optically controlled phased array antenna, and demonstrated the beam steering and the differential radiation beam generation in the received C-band RF signal.

articleTitle: Performance evaluation of in-building radio-over-fiber distribution of multi-band OFDM UWB signals
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: The performance of in building distribution of ultra wideband signals is studied experimentally in a laboratory experiment. Analytical and simulation work is also reported confirming the experimental results. The analysis considers multiband-OFDM radio-over-fiber transmission in 300 m of standard single mode fiber and also in multimode fiber for the shake of comparison. Both optical transmission media exhibit an error vector magnitude limit of -14.5 dB as defined in ECMA-368.

articleTitle: Broadband RF spectrum analyzer based on spectral hole burning
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We investigate a potentially large bandwidth / high resolution RF spectrum analyzer, based on spectral hole burning in Tm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3+</sup>:YAG. With respect to our previous investigations, we strive to take advantage of recent advances in closed cycle cryogenics, fast scanning DFB lasers, and stable mechanical beam deflectors.

articleTitle: Nonlinearly chirped microwave pulse generation using a spatially discrete chirped fiber Bragg grating
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: In this paper, we propose an optical approach to generating nonlinearly chirped microwave pulses based on space-to-frequency-to-time mapping using a spatially discrete chirped fiber Bragg grating (SD-CFBG). The SD-CFBG functions to perform simultaneous spectral slicing, frequency-to-time mapping and temporal shifting. The generation of a nonlinearly chirped microwave pulse with a chirp rate varying from 93.6 to 11.2 GHz/ns is experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Demonstration of 2.5Gb/s optical PSK signal and the ASK wireless transmission based on heterodyne detection in a radio-over-fiber platform
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A novel scheme of 2.5 Gb/s optical PSK signals transmission and ASK wireless signals generation with 15 GHz carrier based on heterodyne detection is demonstrated, which can realize polarization diversity and provide 1.3 Gb/s HDTV applications.

articleTitle: Optical beamforming using chirped fiber grating: Criticality of group delay ripple
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: The effect of group delay ripple on optical beam-formers using chirped fiber grating is investigated in this paper. Optical beam-formers are promised to have many advantages over their electrical beam-forming counter-parts. However, mathematical analyses and simulation results have shown that the group delay ripple causes many limitations on the system performance, especially on the beam direction and directivity. As a result, the most advantageous feature of optical beam-formers using chirped grating, which is squint-free, has to be reconsidered.

articleTitle: A carrier-suppressed phase-modulated fiber optic link with IF downconversion of 30GHz 64-QAM signals
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We develop and demonstrate an efficient, simple fiber optic link for K-band through millimeter-wave signal relay and downconversion. The link uses optical phase modulation to simplify the transmitter and re-modulates the optical carrier with a local oscillator (LO) tone in the receiver, eliminating the need for a second frequency or phase-coherent optical heterodyne source. An optical notch filter in the receiver removes the carrier to allow direct detection of the intermediate frequency (IF). A 30 GHz signal is downconverted to a 140 MHz IF, with a measured noise figure (NF) of 32.5 dB, thirdorder spur-free dynamic range (SFDR) of 112 dB/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sup>, and only 3.5 dB RF conversion loss with 10mA of received DC photocurrent. A 10MBaud 64-QAM signal at 30 GHz is also passed through the link; the IF output has no measureable degradation in error vector magnitude (EVM) from the back-to-back, all-electrical case.

articleTitle: Demonstration of SCM signal transmission based on digitized radio-over-fiber technique
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: In this paper, we propose an effective scheme for a subcarrier-multiplexed (SCM) transmission system based on digitized Radio-over-Fiber (DRoF) technique. We also demonstrate experimentally a tri-band SCM signal transmission over a DRoF link by employing a commercially-available FPGA with satisfactory error-vector-magnitudes of less than 1% at a received optical power of -20dBm.

articleTitle: Crosstalk investigation for optical transport schemes in optical-wireless integrated networks
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We investigate the impact of crosstalk between different optical transport schemes for simultaneous delivery of wired and wireless signals in an optical-wireless integrated access network. Our results show that optical tandem single sideband with optical filtering has the best crosstalk performance while the crosstalk in directly modulated VCSEL has to be carefully managed in order to realize a potentially low-cost transmitter in a hybrid optical-wireless integrated base station.

articleTitle: Opto-electrical predistortion linearization using uncooled DFB-LD for multi-service on broadband radio-over-fiber systems
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We experimentally demonstrated a linear optical transmitter with opto-electrical predistortion method for radio-over-fiber systems. The experimental results show that the significant reduction of about 30 dB in the third-order intermodulation distortion (IMD3) is achieved at 2.4 GHz. For the broad frequency range from 1.97 GHz to 2.48 GHz (510 MHz), IMD3 is enhanced by more than 10 dB.

articleTitle: Tunable laser optical self-heterodyning for QAM modulated frequency-hopped signal generation
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: This paper explores a new approach for the optical generation of frequency agile RF subcarriers. In addition to rapid frequency hopping we demonstrated effective quadrature amplitude modulated (QAM) of the microwave carrier. The approach is compatible with Radio-over-Fiber (RoF) communications and is particularly well suited for applications that require high data rates and security. The research presented here emphasizes proof-of-concept experimentations and addresses the technological requirements to fully exploit its potential.

articleTitle: Push-pull modulated analog photonic link with enhanced SFDR
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We demonstrate an analog photonic link (APL) with a high multioctave spurious-free dynamic range (SFDR) of 120 dB.Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sup> at the frequency of 2.50 GHz. The APL consists of a pair of distributed-feedback laser diodes (DFB LDs), modulated in a push-pull manner, and a balanced photodetector aiming at suppressing the second-order intermodulation distortion (IMD2). At the frequency of 2.50 GHz, an IMD2 suppression of 40 dB, relative to the case of a single arm APL with one laser, is obtained. In a wide frequency range of 600 MHz (2.60 to 3.20 GHz), an improvement of 5 to 18 dB of the second-order SFDR relative to the single arm APL has been achieved.

articleTitle: Using optical nonlinearities to enhance microwave optical links
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Historically, analog fiber optic links have been designed with the goals of high linearity and low noise. Rather than avoid all nonlinear effects, we consider ways that optical nonlinearities can enhance the performance of a microwave optical link, and describe two specific examples.

articleTitle: Low cost bidirectionnal QPSK transmission with optical frequency conversion
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a low cost bidirectional radio-over-fiber system based on the use of a simple p-i-n photodiode (PD) and a VCSEL. PD provides both photodetection and frequency conversion capabilities and its mixing efficiency is evaluated through the measurement of the PD non-linear parameter. The functionality of the RoF up-link and down-link systems is verified experimentally for microwave (MW) subcarrier frequency conversion of a 10 Mbaud QPSK digital signal in the 10 GHz band, measuring conversion gain and error vector magnitude (EVM). The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed bidirectional RoF system performs efficiently without significant distortion on the digitally modulated subcarrier, and could be advantageously used for mm-wave applications.

articleTitle: RF-to-RF characterization of a phased array receive antenna steering system using a novel ring resonator-based integrated photonic beamformer
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A novel ring resonator-based photonic beamformer has been developed for continuous and squint-free control of the reception angle of broadband phased array antenna systems. The core of the system is a ring resonator-based optical beamforming network (OBFN) used for delay synchronization and coherent signal combining. The OBFN is integrated in a single chip realized in CMOS-compatible optical waveguide technology together with an optical sideband filter for single-sideband suppressed-carrier modulation, and an optical carrier reinsertion circuit for balanced coherent detection. This paper demonstrates the system functionality by RF-to-RF measurements of the phase and power responses of the integrated OBFN.

articleTitle: A new loss model and system design method for Radio on Free Space Optical Link
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Radio on Free Space Optical Link (RoFSO) has been developed to realize a cost effective and universal platform for heterogeneous wireless services as same as RoF. This paper proposes a new link loss model for RoFSOL based on a long-term experiment of RoFSO transmission and a total system design method for four types of wireless services.

articleTitle: Downstream wavelength reuse for converged wired/wireless access networks based on saturated semiconductor optical amplifiers and filtering
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A Fabry-Perot based filter enables a low bandwidth saturated SOA to implement a wavelength reuse scheme for upstream links featuring combined transport of wired and wireless signals. The architecture is experimentally demonstrated in this paper.

articleTitle: 622-Mb/s downlink transmission in a fiber-fed 60-GHz wireless system using a CMOS integrated optical receiver
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A fiber-fed 60-GHz wireless system using a CMOS integrated optical receiver for broadband data transmission is demonstrated. The CMOS integrated optical receiver fabricated with 0.13-mum standard CMOS technology consists of CMOS-compatible avalanche photodetector, transimpedance amplifier, offset cancellation circuit, and output buffer. Downlink data transmission of 622-Mb/s BPSK data signals in the 60-GHz band is successfully demonstrated with BER less than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-9</sup> at the incident optical power of -4 dBm.

articleTitle: 2.1 Gbit/s ultra-wide-band transmission over 50-m GI-POF using low-cost VCSEL
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We report record transmission systems of ultra-wideband MB-OFDM signal over 50-m 900-mum core graded-index PMMA POF using low-cost VCSEL at 667 nm. A gross bit rate of 2.1 Gbit/s is achieved with BER < 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-3</sup>.

articleTitle: Multiband ultrawideband pulse generation based on a tunable single bandpass photonic filter and differential detection
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: As far as we know, we present the first optical generator for Multiband UWB pulses that satisfies fully all FFC mask requirements in terms of frequency tunability and spectral efficiency eliminating the baseband component.

articleTitle: Simultaneous RoF transmission of wireless and wired signals using remodulation techique in injection-locked FP-LD
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: The radio over fiber system that transmits different signal simultaneously for wireless and wired network is proposed. A double sideband wireless signal is generated by a 30-GHz RF tone and a 1.25-Gbps digital signal at a Mach-Zehnder modulator. One sideband subcarrier of the wireless signal is re-modulated by a 622-Mbps wired signal with injection-locking technique at a Fabry Perot laser diode. The error free transmission of both the wired and wireless signals is achieved simultaneously for access networks after 23-km standard single mode fiber.

articleTitle: Low cost radio over fiber transceiver using phase signal modulation
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: In this paper we propose a novel photonic transceiver based on the phase modulation of an optical broadband source sliced by an Mach-Zehnder interferometer which is suitable for radio over fiber applications. The SCM data signal is introduced in the optical fiber link by the photonic transceiver at the Central Office. After propagation over 20 km of a dispersive SMF link, a CWDM performs the spectral slicing of the modulated optical signal in order to distribute the SCM data to a number of base stations where the transmitted signals are photodetected and demodulated. The tuning properties of the Mach-Zehnder interferometer structure located in the radio over fiber transceiver enable multiservice distribution through all the WDM channels of the network. A good quality of service is guaranteed for different type of codification formats in a 10 GHz electrical range, as shown by the experimental results.

articleTitle: EAM-SOA-based millimeter-wave frequency up-conversion for radio-over-fiber applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We present an optical scheme for frequency up-conversion at the micro-wave and millimeter-wave bands based on semiconductor optical amplifier. The proposed scheme modulates the bias current with an intermediate frequency (IF) in order to achieve intensity modulation of the incoming optical signal modulated with a local oscillator (LO) frequency. After photo-detection products in the form IF+LO are obtained. An error vector magnitude lower than -29 dB, BER<10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup> for 64-QAM, and a spurious-free dynamic range better than 61 dBmiddotHz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2/3</sup> are measured for an optical input power of -6 dBm.

articleTitle: From digital user to analog airwaves and back
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: This presentation provides an overview of photonic technologies for microwave sensing, transmission, processing, and generation that typically centers on the antenna front end. In this paper illustrate the typical components and subsystems that link the airwaves to the digital user. Actual front-ends may function as a transmitter, a receiver, or both. Modular functionalities include: local oscillator (LO), digital to analog converter (DAC), DeltaPhi/DeltaA phase and amplitude control (beamforming), high power amplifier (HPA), low noise amplifier (LNA), mixer <8>, analog-to-digital converter (ADC), and digital pre and post-conditioning circuits (DT and DR). Photonic technologies and their forward-looking challenges discussed here will include: high-fidelity links, circulators, low phase noise RF oscillators, ADCs, electro-magnetic pulse survivability, integrated circuits, analog signal processing, and antenna elements.

articleTitle: Governing the speed of light: Recent advances and future perspectives of slow and fast light in microwave-photonics
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: The control of the group velocity of optical signals has been widely demonstrated using various optical phenomena and different media. Slow and fast light is achieved in a controllable manner by modifying the refractive index dispersion through light induced modifications of the material or the structural properties of the medium. The potential for a continuous tuning of the phase or time delay of broadband microwave signals modulating the optical carrier opens previously unexplored horizons. The talk will review the recent advancements and the future directions of slow and fast light research with an emphasis on microwave-photonics applications.

articleTitle: Everything converged — A flexible photonic home
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Numerous aspects of home networks, from physical layer and architectures to applications and economics, are described in this paper. Trends and requirements for fiber-in-the-home (FITH) are highlighted.

articleTitle: Demonstration of an indoor real-time location system with optical fibre backbone
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We report the first demontration of an indoor realtime location system, based on an optical fibre backbone, using an active RFID tag emitting 83.5 MHz wide linear FM chirp in the 2.4 GHz ISM band.

articleTitle: Demonstration of distributed antenna system using optical multicast radio-over-fibre links
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A full-duplex, optically amplified, multicast radio-over-fibre DAS is presented. IEEE 802.11 g signals, with an EVM less than 5.6% and throughput of 20 Mbps, are transmitted over the optically amplified DAS.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation of an optically fed phase array for UWB personal area networks
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Experimental results are presented for a 4-element fiber fed UWB array. Beam switching is demonstrated over the frequency range 3-5 GHz.

articleTitle: Impulse radio ultra wide-band over multi-mode fiber for in-home signal distribution
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We propose and experimentally demonstrate a high speed impulse radio ultra wide-band (IR-UWB) wireless link for in-home network signal distribution. The IR-UWB pulse is distributed over a multimode fiber to the transmitter antenna. Wireless transmitted bit-rates of 1 Gbps at 2 m and 2 Gbps at 1.5 m have successfully been demonstrated, with a simple envelope detection scheme. This system is remarkably simple and robust; this makes it very attractive for low-cost applications in short range high-speed wireless links with low radiated power.

articleTitle: Optical beamforming for phased array antennas using stimulated Brillouin Scattering
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We present a technique to use Stimulated Brillouin Scattering processing for RF phase-shift in optical feed networks of phased array antennas. Proof-of-concept experiments of beam steering in a 5-element array are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Experimental demonstration of subcarrier multiplexed quantum key distribution
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We provide for the first time, to our knowledge, an experimental demonstration of the feasibility of Subcarrier Multiplexed Quantum Key Distribution (SCM-QKD).

articleTitle: Optimization of photonic transmit/receive module performance
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Previous publications have described techniques that various researchers at photonic systems, Inc. and elsewhere have used to optimize the performance of analog photonic links. The success of these efforts has made the incorporation of antenna-remoting photonic links into radars and RF communications systems attractive to the designers of such systems. In this paper we show that the simple addition of photonic links to carry signals to and from an RF transmit/receive (Tx/Rx) module, while straightforward, is often not the most beneficial approach because it unnecessarily subjects the inherently broadband photonic components to the same bandwidth limitations as the RF circuitry in the module. If one instead begins with the idea that the broadband photonics technology should be central to the design of the antenna Tx/Rx interface, a completely new architecture emerges - one that not only has greater capabilities than the conventional RF interface, but is simpler as well. As an example of a photonics-based antenna interface design that is simple and yields improved capabilities, we present a Tx-isolating photonic Rx (TIPRX) link that operates over many octaves or even decades of bandwidth while providing 40 dB or more of isolation between the transmit and receive signals. The potential system impact of the TIPRX is that an antenna can receive low-power signals while simultaneously transmitting much higher-power signals.

articleTitle: Accurate and efficient transmission evaluation of wireless signals on radio over fiber links
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: An original and efficient time domain model simulating cost-effective IM-DD Radio over Fiber links carrying wideband signals is proposed and successfully applied in a comprehensive investigation on their feasibility over distances of tens of kilometres.

articleTitle: Photonic temporal differentiator based on polarization modulation in a LiNbO3 phase modulator
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A photonic intensity differentiator is proposed based on polarization modulation. The polarization of a continuous wave (CW) optical carrier is rotated in accordance with an RF signal using a LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> phase modulator. By properly setting a polarizer at the output of the phase modulator, the absolute value of the time derivative of the input RF signal can be obtained. The proposed scheme is experimentally verified for an 8 Gbits/s pulse train. Although the differentiator performance is sensitive to the frequency-dependent V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">π</inf> of the LiNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> phase modulator, the power of the input RF signal as well as the operating optical wavelength can be optimized to get a good performance. The proposed scheme is expected to be able to process higher bit-rate signals when 40 Gb/s optical components are used.

articleTitle: Minimizing photodiode nonlinearities by compensating voltage-dependent responsivity effects
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Two voltage-dependant responsivity effects, impact ionization and Franz-Keldysh oscillations, are shown to have opposing effects at certain wavelengths in p-i-n photodiodes. It is shown that these two effects can compensate each other and minimize photodiode nonlinearities when optimized with respect to wavelength and bias voltage.

articleTitle: Fabry-Perot-based bimodal fiber laser for microwave carrier generation
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We propose a Fabry-Perot-based bimodal fiber laser by cascading up to four fiber-Bragg-gratings (FBG) inside a fiber loop cavity. The adjustment of the relative position between the FBGs enabled us to enhance the finesse of the optical peaks in the transmission spectrum and, consequently, to obtain narrower RF carriers, suitable for use in modern microwave photonic links.

articleTitle: Nested loop feedforward linearization of directly modulated laser diode
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A nested loop feedforward linearization scheme is applied to an uncooled laser diode. This scheme in effect performs linearization twice, thus leading to further reduction of third-order intermodulation products when compared to conventional feedforward linearization. Results are presented for a DFB laser transmitter operating within the 2.4 GHz ISM band. For a two-tone spacing of 20 MHz and 10 dBm input power, conventional feedforward linearization results in third-order intermodulation products at -32.5 dBc as compared to -46.5 dBc for the nested scheme. However, the latter topology requires four cancellation loops as opposed to two for conventional feedforward. As a compromise solution, one of the loops is removed from the nested structure in order to reduce the component count, and in this case third-order intermodulation products are at -43.5 dBc, which is an acceptable trade-off between complexity and distortion reduction.

articleTitle: Instantaneous microwave frequency measurement using an asymmetric non-linear group delay profile
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Instantaneous microwave frequency measurement with adjustable measurement range and resolution is demonstrated using a single non-linearly chirped fibre Bragg grating. Frequency measurement with good accuracy is experimentally realized with a compact setup.

articleTitle: Tunable microwave signal generation using dual-wavelength DFB erbium-doped fiber laser
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A tunable dual-wavelength distributed feedback fiber laser is presented. By controlling two phase shifts induced dynamically in the grating of the laser cavity, a 7 GHz tuning range of a microwave photomixed signal is obtained.

articleTitle: Optical RF instantaneous frequency measurement form Stokes parameters
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A technique to RF instantaneous frequency measurement is proposed and experimentally demonstrate. The architecture presented is based on single sideband modulation with suppressed carrier (SSB-SC) and the change in the Stokes parameters at the output of a birefringent medium. Preliminary results show errors below 50 MHz in the 57% of measurement carried out.

articleTitle: Full colorless gigabit WDM-passive optical network with simultaneous two different signal transmission
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A new wavelength division multiplexed-passive optical network (WDM-PON) scheme supporting the transmission of heterogeneous data as well as broadcast signal is proposed. Both an optical carrier suppression and multiplexing of arrayed waveguide grating (AWG) with 50-GHz channel spacing are employed to generate each optical carrier for the transmission of these data. A reflective semiconductor optical amplifier (RSOA) is also used so that this architecture operates irrespective of wavelength. In case of downlink transmission, error-free transmissions (BER of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-11</sup>) of 1.25-Gb/s and 2.5-Gb/s baseband data are achieved at the same time. Also, 64-quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) signal of 60 Mb/s is transmitted showing the error vector magnitude (EVM) of 4.7 % in the presence of the transmission of 2.5-Gb/s baseband data.

articleTitle: Bidirectional optical access netwok based on PolMUX tecnique using centralized light sources
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We propose and demonstrate an optical network architecture with centralized light sources by using polarization multiplexing technique. The optical source which transports the downstream signal and the CW optical source which will be used in the remote Base Station are polarization multiplexed in the Central Office. After fiber transmission, both optical signals are polarization demultiplexed in the Base Station where the CW optical source is modulated by the upstream data at the Base Station.

articleTitle: Harmonic distortion in SOA based slow/fast light microwave photonic phase shifters
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We address theoretically and experimentally the generation of harmonic distortion in a SFL phase shifter based on CPO in a SOA device. The topic is of importance in the context of microwave photonics for two reasons. First of all, it provides useful guidelines for the proper design of distortion-free SFL tunable phase shifters. In second place, it allows us to explore for the possibility of designing upconverting devices where the phase of the upconverted signal can be tuned, a unique feature to the best of our knowledge.

articleTitle: Efficient optoelectronic de-embedding for VCSEL intrinsic response extraction
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: In this present work, we propose a new method to remove the parasitics contribution to the VCSEL chip response, in order to obtain the intrinsic transmission behavior. It has been observed that the S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</sub> reflection coefficient of the chip is only due to the electrical access to the chip composed by the transmission line and cavity contacts. This allows us to decompose the chip into two cascaded subsystems representing the electrical access and the optical cavity respectively. An equivalent electrical circuit is developed for the electrical access behavior and, combined with the transfer matrix formalism, it becomes possible to remove the parasitics contribution from the measured S<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</sub> response. In this way, the intrinsic 3-dB bandwidth of the VCSEL can be determined.

articleTitle: Two-polarization two-frequency operation in a class-A semiconductor laser
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Tunable dual-frequency oscillation is demonstrated in a VECSEL using spatial separation of the two orthogonally polarized eigenstates. The VECSEL class-A dynamics enables to get rid of electrical phase noise in excess at relaxation oscillation frequency.

articleTitle: Coherence-free RF/microwave photonic bandpass filter with high skirt selectivity
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A novel coherence-free RF/microwave photonic signal processor based on a frequency-shifting delay line structure with an optical filter is presented. It can realise a high skirt selectivity and high stopband attenuation bandpass filter response.

articleTitle: Overview of present/future needs of MWP for defence system applications
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: For many years, optical-microwave technologies have appeared as promising for numerous applications. Indeed, fibre-based communications are well established nowadays in digital transmission systems. The maturity and the performances of optoelectronic components, in terms of spectral purity and linearity, are such that today they enable optical transmission and processing of analogue broad-bandwidth microwave signals. Moreover, the inherent parallel nature of light, the low sensitivity to electromagnetic perturbations and the capability to perform processing functions in the optical domain allow the introduction of new concepts such as local oscillator distribution, optical beam-forming, adaptive filtering or radar signal and waveform generation. These new concepts are good candidate for application and further validation into ship or ground-based radars, as well as into space or airborne systems.

articleTitle: GHz-multichannel SCM-WDM transmission over multimode fiber links employing an optical broadband source
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: In this paper a new low-cost SCM-WDM scheme suitable for short/middle-reach multimode radio over fiber applications is proposed. The approach is based on the spectral slicing of an optical broadband source centred at 1550 nm and a Mach-Zehnder interferometric structure used to increase the operative frequency range up to 20 GHz. Free-error transmission for QPSK and 64-QAM digital signals over a 20 GHz SCM bandwidth is experimentally demonstrated making the proposed low-cost architecture suitable for future PONs.

articleTitle: Uni-traveling-carrier balanced photodiode with tunable MMI coupler for optimization of source laser RIN suppression
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A balanced uni-traveling-carrier (UTC) waveguide photodiode (PD) has been fabricated and characterized. The balanced PD incorporates a multimode interference (MMI) coupler as a light combiner/splitter with tunability of the output power splitting ratio. The individual UTC-PDs demonstrate a 1 dB compression current of 80.5 mA and a third-order output intercept point of 46.1 dBm at 60 mA, both representing the highest reported for a waveguide PD. The ability to fine tune the output power splitting of the MMI coupler allows for optimization of source laser relative-intensity noise suppression.

articleTitle: Photodiode limitations in the generation of low-noise microwave signals from stable frequency combs
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: An optically-stabilized femtosecond laser frequency comb can generate low phase noise microwave signals; however, excess noise arises in the photodetection process. We study the impact of photodetector shot noise, saturation, and power-top phase conversion on 1-10 GHz signal generation.

articleTitle: Performance of MB-OFDM UWB and WiMAX IEEE 802.16e converged radio-over-fiber in PON
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Experimental results about the performance of converged radio-over- fiber transmission including multiband-OFDM UWB and WiMAX 802.16 e wireless over a passive optical network are reported in this paper. The experimental study indicates that UWB and WiMAX converged transmission is feasible over the proposed distribution set-up employing a single wavelength. However, the results indicate that there is an EVM penalty of 3.2 dB for a UWB 10 km SSMF transmission in presence of WiMAX wireless.

articleTitle: Simplification of the central station in a millimeter-wave radio-on-fiber system using wavelength-tunable light sources to switch base stations
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a novel system configuration to simplify a central station in a millimeter-wave radio-on-fiber system. Optical wavelength paths are switched using tunable light sources and required devices can be reduced.

articleTitle: Photonic arbitrary waveform generator
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: An arbitrary waveform generator is demonstrated using WDM fiber-optic components. Cross-gain modulation method in a semiconductor optical amplifier is implemented to convert 3-bit digital words to an arbitrary analog waveform at a rate of 3 Gb/s.

articleTitle: Novel generation and transmission of FCC-compliant impulse radio ultra wideband signals over 100-m GI-POF
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: We demonstrate a novel technique for generation and transmission of IR-UWB signals over 100-m 50-mum core GI-POF. IR-UWB pulses are made by linearly combining two first-order derivatives of Gaussian pulses with different pulse-shaping factors.

articleTitle: Photonic UWB pulse generation compatible with dymanic capacity allocation in access network
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A monocycle Ultra-Wideband (UWB) pulse generator based on 2-tap microwave photonic filter with phase inversion is proposed. The microwave filter is fed by two lasers and uses phase inversion in a Mach-Zehnder modulator to generate negative coefficients. The proposed UWB pulse generator incorporates a variable delay line to compensate the effects of the chromatic dispersion over the generated UWB pulse which can be transmitted through an optical network where dynamic assignment capacity is implemented.

articleTitle: Quantum formalism for electrooptic modulators
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: In this paper we provide the basic formalism describing the evolution of quantum coherent states in arbitrary electro-optic modulators subject to RF modulation. We then use the (overcomplete) basis of coherent states to infer the evolution of single-photon quantum states as the simplest representatives of quantum states without classical limit.

articleTitle: Discrete time microwave photonic transversal filter
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: A novel transversal filtering based on discrete time optical processing is proposed. We demonstrate a two tap filter with 37 dB extinction, excellent stability and signal to noise ratio.

articleTitle: Program at a glance
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: Provides a schedule of conference events and a listing of which papers were presented in each session.

abstract: Presents the front inside cover of the proceedings record.

articleTitle: [Front cover]
publicationTitle: 2009 International Topical Meeting on Microwave Photonics
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: silicon and III-V integration for microwave photonics; devices for broadband applications; microwave photonic signal processing; radio-over-fibre systems.
